about: Homes and students: the town’s single-family parcel count and the schools’ headcount, FY1994 to FY2026, side by side — the town has added homes every year and the schools have not gained children.

conclusions.basis: Single-family parcels from the DLS average tax bill file, Lunenburg rows, FY1994–FY2026; enrolment from `dese_enrollment`, district rows, total_cnt. DLS’s fiscal year is the tax year and DESE’s is the school year; both FY-labels describe the same autumn and are set side by side on that basis.
conclusions.claim: 773 more single-family homes since FY1994, and 319 fewer students than the FY2003 peak.
conclusions.detail: The town has been building. The schools have been shrinking. Both are true in the same years, from two state files that count two different things. Single-family parcels went from 2,872 in FY1994 to 3,645 in FY2026, up 26.9%, and fell in 0 of the 26 year-to-year steps the record holds. Enrolment peaked at 1,887 in FY2003 and stands at 1,568, down 16.9%. The two lines cross the page in opposite directions.

added.unit: more single-family homes, FY1994 to FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: WHY. Fewer children per home, older households, children choicing out, new homes bought by households without children — this pair of series separates none of them. Nor does the homes count include condominiums or apartments; it is single-family parcels only.

see.label: Who is in the schools, FY1994 to today

conclusions.so_what: Homes rose in every one of the 26 steps in the record. Enrolment has not followed them.

conclusions.basis: The two series above, divided, year by year.
conclusions.claim: 43.0 students for every hundred single-family homes in FY2026, against 61.2 in FY1994.
conclusions.detail: Dividing one series by the other gives students per hundred homes: 61.2 in FY1994, 43.0 in FY2026, a fall of 29.7%. It is a ratio of two counts and not a household survey: it does not say which homes hold children.
conclusions.not_shown: Children per household. The Census publishes households with a child under 18 only as a five-year sample (on /lunenburg-by-the-numbers), so the ratio here is homes to students, not families to children.

see.label: A third of homes have a child under 18 — the five-year sample

conclusions.so_what: Fewer school-age children for each home than the town had. The fact under every “growth” argument.

conclusions.basis: The same two series, the latest six fiscal years.
conclusions.claim: In the last five years: +87 single-family homes, −25 students.
conclusions.detail: FY2021 to FY2026: single-family parcels 3,558 to 3,645, enrolment 1,593 to 1,568. A new home in Lunenburg has not, on this record, meant a new pupil.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the homes added were bought by families with children who then enrolled elsewhere — Monty Tech, school choice, private school — which would leave enrolment flat with more children in town. /where-students-go-instead counts residents educated elsewhere and is the place to look.

see.label: What commercial growth would have to look like

conclusions.so_what: Building does not read through to enrolment on any horizon this record shows — five years or twenty.

grain: Two COUNTS on two state files: single-family parcels as DLS reports them each fiscal year, and children enrolled in the district on 1 October. Neither is a dollar figure; neither says who lives in a home.
not_established: Why enrolment does not follow homes: children per household, the age of households moving in, and children educated outside the district are three explanations this pair of counts cannot separate.
How many homes of other kinds — condominiums, apartments, two-family — were added; the DLS series is single-family parcels only.
School-age children per household by year. The Census gives it as a five-year sample; the assessors’ records carry no ages.

sources.note: Every town’s single-family parcels by fiscal year, exported from the DLS Gateway by script. The parcel count is the homes series here.
